applies_to: Trane CGAM air-cooled scroll chillers whose Symbio 800 points list Trane tags '(CH530)'.
summary: A short list of 72 BACnet objects for CGAM chillers, using low instance numbers and output objects for the BAS commands: AO for chilled water, hot water, heat recovery and demand limit setpoints, BO for auto/stop, diagnostic reset, noise reduction and heat recovery enable, and MO for the chiller mode. There are no per-alarm diagnostic objects; BI 23 Alarm Present is the summary alarm.
notes: The tables have no read/write column: AI/BI/MI are read-only, and the AO/BO/MO objects are the BAS commands and setpoints, marked writable here.

Trane titles this list 'CGAM (CH530)' and does not explain the suffix in the document. This list uses short instance numbers (AI 1, AO 1, BO 1...) unlike the standard Symbio 800 CGAM list (BAS-PTS019) with 5-digit instances and AV/BV/MV commands, so check which list matches the controller on site.
Units are listed as a quantity (Temperature, Pressure, Percent...); the communicated engineering unit follows the factory-configured unit system (I-P or SI), not the web UI display setting.
AO and BO/MO tables give relinquish defaults, shown in the AO descriptions (e.g. chilled water setpoint default 44°F).
MI 3 MP Communication Status is marked 'Do Not Use This Point' in the doc.
The Symbio 800 integration guide (BAS-SVP083) covers BACnet IP and BACnet MS/TP; the rotary address sets the MS/TP MAC and a default Device ID of 1-127, and a software Device ID can be set instead.

source.title: Symbio 800 Integration Points List BACnet - CGAM (CH530)

integration.summary: Put the chiller on the network (BACnet MS/TP or IP), then write the auto/stop command, chilled water setpoint, demand limit and mode. Read back running state, leaving water temperature and capacity. Check the local-setpoint flag to confirm the BAS setpoints are actually in use. The commands are AO/BO/MO objects; everything else is read-only status.

minimum_points.name: Chilled Water Setpoint
minimum_points.why: Chilled water setpoint from the BMS

minimum_points.name: Local Setpoint Control
minimum_points.why: Shows if local setpoints override BAS setpoints

minimum_points.name: Alarm Present
minimum_points.why: Any active alarm on the chiller

integration.enable: BO 1 Chiller Auto Stop Command (Inactive = Stop, Active = Auto; relinquish default Auto) is the BMS auto/stop; with it at Auto the chiller runs when its own run conditions are met. BI 1 Run Enabled shows whether the chiller is enabled to run. The documents don't say how the two combine or how to hand setpoint control to the BAS; BI 2 Local Setpoint Control shows when the chiller is using local setpoints instead of BAS setpoints.
setup: With no protocol specified at order, the controller ships as BACnet MS/TP at 76,800 bps with the rotary address at 000, and MS/TP is disabled at 000. Set a rotary address of 001-127 to bring it online.
The rotary address sets the MS/TP MAC and the Device ID and takes effect without a power cycle. A software Device ID (1-4194302) can be set in the web UI, Tracer SC+ or Tracer TU.
The web UI is reached only over USB at http://198.80.18.1/; the Ethernet ports do not serve it.
BACnet IP uses Ethernet port 1 (or the optional USB Wi-Fi adapter); the default UDP port is 47808. Enable BBMD only if this is the only BACnet IP device on the subnet, then fill in the BDT.
MS/TP wiring lands on the P1 link; P2 and P3 are for factory devices only, and Ethernet port 2 is only for the touch-screen display.
gotchas: Communicated units (I-P or SI) are fixed at the factory; changing them in the field needs a Trane representative. Web UI display units do not change the BACnet values.
Points that don't apply to the unit's configuration are absent, and a technician can 'recycle' (remove) factory points from the interface, so a missing object may have been recycled.
This list has no read/write column; writability of the AO/BO/MO objects is inferred from their object type and relinquish defaults.
Diagnostic BIs are one object per alarm condition and only exist for the options fitted.
The commands are output objects (AO/BO/MO), not the AV/BV/MV objects used on the standard Symbio 800 CGAM list, so a template from that list won't map.
BO 1 relinquishes to Auto, so releasing the BMS command lets the chiller run if its own conditions are met.
